- Capacity created ahead of time with sufficient spare capacity maintained to absorb surge orders from customers
- Online instant-quote portal where customers upload a drawing and secure an instant quote, against an industry norm where most suppliers take weeks for a basic quotation
- World's largest installed capacity for metal injection molding, with more than one million square feet of manufacturing floor space

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Currency / foreign-exchange risk on an export-led, import-dependent model — A very significant portion of revenue comes from exports while all raw materials and most capital goods and spares are imported, so the Company's financials are structurally exposed to the rupee. Management names this as its 'Weakness'. The natural hedge from being a USD-surplus company is only partial: policy is to cover up to about 50% of net currency exposure with plain forwards, and in FY26 coverage was deliberately kept far below 50% on a directional view that the rupee would depreciate - a discretionary position that gains when the rupee falls and loses when it does not.
- Raw material price risk on a fully imported raw-material base — The Company imports all its raw materials, carrying both a currency leg and a price leg. In FY26 the raw material price per kilogram went up marginally with no major price shock, but the structural exposure to imported input prices remains and is not hedged separately from the currency cover.
- Customer credit and receivables risk — Management runs a rigorous credit control policy with fortnightly receivables reviews to identify stressed accounts ahead of time, helped by being the sole supplier to most of its customers and by long-standing relationships. Management explicitly states that while these measures can minimise the risk, they cannot eliminate it completely.
- Cybersecurity and IT business-continuity risk - a ransomware breach already occurred — The Company runs on its IT systems and treats failure or non-availability as a major risk. Despite firewalls and security systems, there was a breach of the firewall from a ransomware attack in August 2025; there was no loss of customer data but the systems had to be reconstructed under the established security protocol and were back in full operation within a few days. Mitigation since includes daily on-site backups, an offsite backup server, a more rigorous Cyber Administration system and a start on securing a cyber-risk insurance policy.
- End-market concentration in cyclical and regulated verticals — Revenue is concentrated in Automotive, Defence, Medical, Aerospace and Consumer Products. Management asserts the diversified customer and industry base reduces dependence on any single end-use industry, but the Company provides no segment-wise or product-wise reporting, so the actual concentration within these end-uses is not visible to an outside reader.
- Execution and regulatory risk on the new Chennai plant and the arms-components venture — Manufacturing operations have only just commenced at the new Chennai plant, and the licensable firearm components business to be run through INDO-MIM Arms Components Private Limited depends on a Ministry of Home Affairs manufacturing licence that had not yet been applied for as at the report - the Company states it 'would make necessary application ... shortly'. Revenue from this vertical is gated on an approval outside the Company's control.
- Loss-making overseas subsidiaries and acquisition-integration risk — The Company has grown capacity inorganically (TRIAX Industries LLC in FY21, Conway Marsh Garrett Technologies in June 2023, Phoenix DeVentures II Inc in 2025) and states an intent to venture further into allied technologies organically or by acquisition. Form AOC-1 shows several of these wholly owned subsidiaries carrying losses before taxation, so integration and turnaround of acquired units is a live structural exposure.
- Natural calamity and physical asset risk — Machinery, stock and premises are insured against fire and other natural calamities and stock in transit is covered by a marine policy, with the coverage considered adequate; the Company notes its facilities are not located in an identified natural calamity zone. The exposure is mitigated by insurance rather than eliminated.

business.body: Formed in 1996, INDO-MIM Limited is a fully integrated precision engineering components manufacturer providing end-to-end manufacturing solutions, primarily using Metal Injection Molding (MIM), alongside precision investment casting, precision machining, ceramic injection molding, additive manufacturing / 3D printing, metal powder manufacturing and electronics components manufacturing and assembly. It has proven proficiency across design, tooling, materials, finishing and assembly operations, and supplies complex-shaped precision components and sub-assemblies to customers across Automotive, Defence, Medical, Aerospace and Consumer Products end-uses, plus other products and services such as metal powders, tooling and traded products. - Strengthen its position as a global precision manufacturing solutions provider by leveraging expertise across MIM, investment casting, precision machining, ceramic injection molding and additive manufacturing

outlook.body: INDO-MIM's manufacturing footprint spans more than one million square feet of floor space, housing what the Company describes as the world's largest installed capacity for metal injection molding. MIM manufacturing runs from Hoskote and Doddaballapur in the KIADB Industrial Area near Bangalore, Karnataka, and investment casting from the APIIC Industrial Park at Chittoor/Tirupathi, Andhra Pradesh. The most significant addition in FY26 is a new plant at Chennai, Tamil Nadu, where manufacturing operations have just now commenced; the Chennai site sits in the Defence and Aerospace Zone and will also house the manufacturing facility being put up for the licensable firearm components business to be run through the newly formed wholly owned subsidiary INDO-MIM Arms Components Private Limited (incorporated December 2025), for which the Company says it would make the necessary application to the Ministry of Home Affairs to secure a manufacturing licence shortly. Internationally, wholly owned subsidiary INDO-MIM INC runs a MIM manufacturing unit in San Antonio, Texas, USA, and a step-down associate in Mexico (49% held by INDO-MIM INC) handles post-manufacturing secondary operations. Capacity has also been added inorganically: TRIAX Industries LLC, USA (casting and machining) acquired during FY21, Conway Marsh Garrett Technologies Limited, UK (MIM components) acquired in June 2023, and Phoenix DeVentures II Inc, USA (medical device prototype manufacturing and design) acquired in May 2025. The Company states its practice is to create capacity ahead of time and maintain sufficient spare capacity to address surge orders from customers, and that it desires to venture into other allied and ancillary technologies in the days to come, either organically or by inorganic acquisition of other companies. No specific investment was made for the sake of energy conservation, and the Company has not quantified separately the investment made in replacing energy-inefficient equipment as part of its continuous improvement projects.

outlook.body:
- Increasing adoption of precision-engineered components across diverse industries, coupled with the continuing shift towards lightweight, complex and high-performance components, provides opportunities for sustained long-term growth
- The global manufacturing environment continues to evolve with increasing emphasis on precision, miniaturization, lightweighting, cost efficiency, material optimization and supply-chain resilience, expected to support adoption of MIM and other near-net-shape processes
- Increasing requirement for components with complex geometries and tighter dimensional tolerances is expected to create further opportunities for MIM adoption across several industries
- Increasing preference of global customers for reliable and integrated manufacturing partners provides a favourable long-term environment for the business
- Automotive: increasing vehicle complexity, demand for lightweight components, enhanced safety requirements and the evolution of electric and technologically advanced vehicles are expected to create opportunities for precision-engineered components
- Defence: increasing emphasis on domestic manufacturing, indigenization of defence components and development of advanced defence systems is expected to support demand
- Medical: increasing demand for sophisticated medical devices, surgical instruments and other precision components keeps the sector a key focus area
- Aerospace: increasing requirement for lightweight, high-precision and technically advanced components presents significant long-term opportunities in the evolving aerospace supply chain
- Management expects the online instant-quote system to significantly drive the business in days to come

business_ops.seasonality: The DRHP states that seasonality, including the variability of shipments under large contracts, customers' seasonal orders and variations in product mix, affects many aspects of the business, and that negative seasonal factors could have an adverse effect on business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows. It further notes that the global manufacturing industry has historically been subject to cyclical fluctuations resulting from sector-specific dynamics (changes in technology, government regulation and end-consumer preference) as well as from changes in general economic conditions. Customer arrangements are typically open or discreet purchase orders without binding volume commitments, with rolling forecasts or indicative schedules subject to revision, exposing the Company to fluctuations in order volumes, procurement timelines and product mix. No quantified seasonality (quarter-wise or month-wise) split is disclosed.
business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward-integrated, dual-shore manufacturing. The integrated set-up covers the MIM manufacturing process together with in-house secondary processes for MIM components, and vertically integrated finishing technologies including electroless nickel and trivalent chromium plating, vacuum and sealed quench heat-treating, precision grinding and CNC machining to micron tolerances. In-house capabilities extend upstream to mold designing and tooling (45 to 50 new tools produced per month) and downstream to plastic injection and insert molding, product assembly and integration services, so the Company offers end-to-end solutions from mold design through finished, surface-treated components. As part of its backward integration strategy the Company has initiated manufacturing of stainless-steel powder and is in the process of establishing an iron powder manufacturing facility at Gowribidanur Industrial Area, Chikkaballapur, Karnataka, targeted by end of Fiscal 2027; it states it will continue developing backward integration capabilities to provide more material options to customers (over 80 alloying options as of March 31, 2026). Manufacturing is dual-shore across India, the United States, the United Kingdom and Mexico across five technologies (metal injection molding, ceramic injection molding, investment casting, precision machining and metal 3D printing), with facilities described as fungible across sectors. On the inbound side there is no integration: all raw materials (metal powders such as carbonyl iron and stainless steel, and polymers including polypropylene, wax and stearic acid) are imported and procured on a purchase-order basis with no long-term supply contracts; imports were 60.95%, 61.80% and 59.63% of total raw material purchases in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, and the top 10 suppliers accounted for 42.91%, 29.55% and 44.68% of total raw material purchase cost. Cost of materials consumed was 20.87%, 17.52% and 15.68% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. Downstream the Company sells direct to OEMs through three sales offices (China, Germany, United States) and 13 sales representatives across nine other countries.

Indo Mim is a genuine global category leader (world's largest MIM manufacturer, 6.8% global MIM revenue share held six years) with, on this RHP's FY2024-FY2026 restated numbers, clean and accelerating growth (revenue ~20.9% CAGR, PAT ~37% CAGR, EPS Rs 5.89 -> Rs 11.06), improving return ratios (RoNW 14.0% -> 21.3%) and operating cash flow ahead of PAT every year. The equity story is qualified by a predominantly Offer-for-Sale structure with a modest Fresh Issue directed at debt repayment rather than growth capex, high export/tariff exposure (~77-90% of revenue), elevated leverage (~Rs 1,090 cr) with a sharply higher FY26 finance cost, and a cluster of governance/record-keeping items. Consistent, accelerating growth: revenue from operations Rs 2,870.40 cr (FY24) -> Rs 3,329.58 cr (FY25) -> Rs 4,192.99 cr (FY26), ~20.9% two-year CAGR; PAT Rs 283.73 cr -> Rs 423.73 cr -> Rs 533.54 cr, ~37% CAGR; basic EPS Rs 5.89 -> Rs 8.79 -> Rs 11.06.
Strong operating cash conversion: CFO exceeded PAT in all three years - FY26 CFO Rs 1,077.24 cr vs PAT Rs 533.54 cr; FY25 Rs 506.27 cr vs Rs 423.73 cr; FY24 Rs 458.33 cr vs Rs 283.73 cr.

Diversified end-markets and geographies: FY26 revenue across Automotive 24.61%, Defence 18.69%, Medical 18.08%, Aerospace 11.96% and Consumer 10.80%; exports ~77% of revenue supplied to customers in 55 countries; certifications include NADCAP, IATF 16949, AS 9100 and ISO 13485.

Backward-integrated, dual-shore manufacturing: 15 facilities (6 India, 6 US, 2 UK, 1 Mexico) combining India's cost base with US/UK/Mexico proximity to Western OEMs; in-house metal-powder production and end-to-end tooling.
Reducing customer concentration: top-1 customer fell from 13.69% (FY24) to 7.97% (FY26) of revenue and top-10 from 42.00% to 38.41%.

Deleveraging Fresh Issue with clean pledge hygiene: the entire Rs 500 cr Fresh Issue (Rs 400 cr earmarked to prepay borrowings) reduces consolidated debt of Rs 1,212.35 cr (May 31, 2026); nil promoter shares pledged and no bonus within 18 months of the Offer.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: INDO-MIM is a Bangalore-headquartered global precision engineering components manufacturer that houses the world's largest installed capacity for metal injection molding and supplies customers in more than forty-five countries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Formed in 1996, INDO-MIM Limited is a fully integrated precision engineering components manufacturer providing end-to-end manufacturing solutions, primarily using Metal Injection Molding (MIM), alongside precision investment casting, precision machining, ceramic injection molding, additive manufacturing / 3D printing, metal powder manufacturing and electronics components manufacturing and assembly. It has proven proficiency across design, tooling, materials, finishing and assembly operations, and supplies complex-shaped precision components and sub-assemblies to customers across Automotive, Defence, Medical, Aerospace and Consumer Products end-uses, plus other products and services such as metal powders, tooling and traded products. The Company states its diversified customer and industry base reduces dependence on any single end-use industry, and accordingly it provides no segment-wise or product-wise reporting.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- INDO-MIM INC — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100%), USA; runs a MIM manufacturing unit in San Antonio, Texas and holds the 49% stake in the Mexico associate. Related-party counterparty for sale of goods, purchase of sales-commission services and sale of property, plant and equipment, all on ongoing contracts.
- TRIAX Industries LLC — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100%), USA; acquired in September 2020 / during FY21; manufactures parts and components using casting and machining. Related-party counterparty for sale of goods on an ongoing contract.
- Conway Marsh Garrett Technologies Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100%), UK; acquired in June 2023; manufactures components using MIM technology. Related-party counterparty for sale of goods and purchase of goods on ongoing contracts.
- Phoenix DeVentures II INC — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100%), USA; acquired in March 2025 (the MD&A states May 2025); engaged in medical device prototype manufacturing and design. Related-party counterparty for purchase of goods on an ongoing contract.
- INDO-MIM Arms Components Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (99.99% shareholding per Form AOC-1), India; incorporated in December 2025 to conduct all licensable firearm components business, with its facility being put up at the Chennai plant in the Defence and Aerospace Zone; first reporting period December to March.
- INDO-MIM MEXICO — associate: Step-down associate company in Mexico, 49% equity held by INDO-MIM INC, USA; handles post-manufacturing secondary operations.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward-integrated, dual-shore manufacturing. The integrated set-up covers the MIM manufacturing process together with in-house secondary processes for MIM components, and vertically integrated finishing technologies including electroless nickel and trivalent chromium plating, vacuum and sealed quench heat-treating, precision grinding and CNC machining to micron tolerances. In-house capabilities extend upstream to mold designing and tooling (45 to 50 new tools produced per month) and downstream to plastic injection and insert molding, product assembly and integration services, so the Company offers end-to-end solutions from mold design through finished, surface-treated components. As part of its backward integration strategy the Company has initiated manufacturing of stainless-steel powder and is in the process of establishing an iron powder manufacturing facility at Gowribidanur Industrial Area, Chikkaballapur, Karnataka, targeted by end of Fiscal 2027; it states it will continue developing backward integration capabilities to provide more material options to customers (over 80 alloying options as of March 31, 2026). Manufacturing is dual-shore across India, the United States, the United Kingdom and Mexico across five technologies (metal injection molding, ceramic injection molding, investment casting, precision machining and metal 3D printing), with facilities described as fungible across sectors. On the inbound side there is no integration: all raw materials (metal powders such as carbonyl iron and stainless steel, and polymers including polypropylene, wax and stearic acid) are imported and procured on a purchase-order basis with no long-term supply contracts; imports were 60.95%, 61.80% and 59.63% of total raw material purchases in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, and the top 10 suppliers accounted for 42.91%, 29.55% and 44.68% of total raw material purchase cost. Cost of materials consumed was 20.87%, 17.52% and 15.68% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. Downstream the Company sells direct to OEMs through three sales offices (China, Germany, United States) and 13 sales representatives across nine other countries.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Increasing adoption of precision-engineered components across diverse industries, coupled with the continuing shift towards lightweight, complex and high-performance components, provides opportunities for sustained long-term growth
- The global manufacturing environment continues to evolve with increasing emphasis on precision, miniaturization, lightweighting, cost efficiency, material optimization and supply-chain resilience, expected to support adoption of MIM and other near-net-shape processes
- Increasing requirement for components with complex geometries and tighter dimensional tolerances is expected to create further opportunities for MIM adoption across several industries
- Increasing preference of global customers for reliable and integrated manufacturing partners provides a favourable long-term environment for the business
- Automotive: increasing vehicle complexity, demand for lightweight components, enhanced safety requirements and the evolution of electric and technologically advanced vehicles are expected to create opportunities for precision-engineered components
- Defence: increasing emphasis on domestic manufacturing, indigenization of defence components and development of advanced defence systems is expected to support demand
- Medical: increasing demand for sophisticated medical devices, surgical instruments and other precision components keeps the sector a key focus area
- Aerospace: increasing requirement for lightweight, high-precision and technically advanced components presents significant long-term opportunities in the evolving aerospace supply chain
- Management expects the online instant-quote system to significantly drive the business in days to come

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Strengthen its position as a global precision manufacturing solutions provider by leveraging expertise across MIM, investment casting, precision machining, ceramic injection molding and additive manufacturing
- Automotive: leverage manufacturing capability and engineering expertise to develop components for evolving automotive applications, while improving product quality, manufacturing efficiency and customer responsiveness and expanding presence in value-added applications
- Defence: further develop capabilities for specialised defence requirements where precision, strength, dimensional accuracy, reliability and repeatability are critical, and strengthen customer relationships to participate in the increasing localisation of defence manufacturing
- Medical: continue developing sector capabilities and work closely with customers during product development and commercialisation of high-precision components
- Aerospace: enhance aerospace manufacturing capabilities, maintain stringent quality standards and develop relationships with customers requiring specialised precision components
- Route the licensable firearm components business through the new wholly owned subsidiary INDO-MIM Arms Components Private Limited, with the facility at the Chennai plant in the Defence and Aerospace Zone and an MHA manufacturing licence to be applied for shortly
- Venture into other allied and ancillary technologies, either organically or through inorganic acquisition of other companies
- Focus R&D on material and process development, targeting process improvement, cost reduction, supplier diversification, supplier substitution and absorption of new technologies
- Create capacity ahead of time and maintain spare capacity to absorb surge orders, sustaining speed of quote, sample submission, production and delivery as the market differentiator
- Scale the online instant-quote portal, where customers upload a drawing and receive an instant quote, as a business driver

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: INDO-MIM's manufacturing footprint spans more than one million square feet of floor space, housing what the Company describes as the world's largest installed capacity for metal injection molding. MIM manufacturing runs from Hoskote and Doddaballapur in the KIADB Industrial Area near Bangalore, Karnataka, and investment casting from the APIIC Industrial Park at Chittoor/Tirupathi, Andhra Pradesh. The most significant addition in FY26 is a new plant at Chennai, Tamil Nadu, where manufacturing operations have just now commenced; the Chennai site sits in the Defence and Aerospace Zone and will also house the manufacturing facility being put up for the licensable firearm components business to be run through the newly formed wholly owned subsidiary INDO-MIM Arms Components Private Limited (incorporated December 2025), for which the Company says it would make the necessary application to the Ministry of Home Affairs to secure a manufacturing licence shortly. Internationally, wholly owned subsidiary INDO-MIM INC runs a MIM manufacturing unit in San Antonio, Texas, USA, and a step-down associate in Mexico (49% held by INDO-MIM INC) handles post-manufacturing secondary operations. Capacity has also been added inorganically: TRIAX Industries LLC, USA (casting and machining) acquired during FY21, Conway Marsh Garrett Technologies Limited, UK (MIM components) acquired in June 2023, and Phoenix DeVentures II Inc, USA (medical device prototype manufacturing and design) acquired in May 2025. The Company states its practice is to create capacity ahead of time and maintain sufficient spare capacity to address surge orders from customers, and that it desires to venture into other allied and ancillary technologies in the days to come, either organically or by inorganic acquisition of other companies. No specific investment was made for the sake of energy conservation, and the Company has not quantified separately the investment made in replacing energy-inefficient equipment as part of its continuous improvement projects.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Speed as the core differentiator - speed in quote, sample submission, production and delivery, with quotes submitted against an RFQ before a competitor even asks for clarification on the drawings
- Capacity created ahead of time with sufficient spare capacity maintained to absorb surge orders from customers
- Online instant-quote portal where customers upload a drawing and secure an instant quote, against an industry norm where most suppliers take weeks for a basic quotation
- World's largest installed capacity for metal injection molding, with more than one million square feet of manufacturing floor space
- Fully integrated supplier across design, tooling, materials, finishing and assembly - a one-stop solution for complex-shaped precision components and sub-assemblies
- Sole-supplier position with most customers and multi-year customer relationships, which supports credit discipline and customer stickiness
- Broad technology portfolio spanning MIM, ceramic injection molding, investment casting, precision machining, powder manufacturing, 3D printing and electronics assembly, with 85+ material options
- Diversified end-use industry and customer base (650+ customers globally, 10000 parts) that reduces dependence on any single end-use industry
- Multi-standard accreditation stack (ISO 9001, IATF 16949, ISO 13485, ISO 14001, AS 9100, ISO 45001) qualifying it for automotive, medical and aerospace supply
- Natural currency hedge as a USD-surplus exporter whose raw materials, most capital goods and spares are imported
- Over 2500 skilled engineers, technicians and manufacturing associates

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Currency / foreign-exchange risk on an export-led, import-dependent model — A very significant portion of revenue comes from exports while all raw materials and most capital goods and spares are imported, so the Company's financials are structurally exposed to the rupee. Management names this as its 'Weakness'. The natural hedge from being a USD-surplus company is only partial: policy is to cover up to about 50% of net currency exposure with plain forwards, and in FY26 coverage was deliberately kept far below 50% on a directional view that the rupee would depreciate - a discretionary position that gains when the rupee falls and loses when it does not.
- Raw material price risk on a fully imported raw-material base — The Company imports all its raw materials, carrying both a currency leg and a price leg. In FY26 the raw material price per kilogram went up marginally with no major price shock, but the structural exposure to imported input prices remains and is not hedged separately from the currency cover.
- Customer credit and receivables risk — Management runs a rigorous credit control policy with fortnightly receivables reviews to identify stressed accounts ahead of time, helped by being the sole supplier to most of its customers and by long-standing relationships. Management explicitly states that while these measures can minimise the risk, they cannot eliminate it completely.
- Cybersecurity and IT business-continuity risk - a ransomware breach already occurred — The Company runs on its IT systems and treats failure or non-availability as a major risk. Despite firewalls and security systems, there was a breach of the firewall from a ransomware attack in August 2025; there was no loss of customer data but the systems had to be reconstructed under the established security protocol and were back in full operation within a few days. Mitigation since includes daily on-site backups, an offsite backup server, a more rigorous Cyber Administration system and a start on securing a cyber-risk insurance policy.
- End-market concentration in cyclical and regulated verticals — Revenue is concentrated in Automotive, Defence, Medical, Aerospace and Consumer Products. Management asserts the diversified customer and industry base reduces dependence on any single end-use industry, but the Company provides no segment-wise or product-wise reporting, so the actual concentration within these end-uses is not visible to an outside reader.
- Execution and regulatory risk on the new Chennai plant and the arms-components venture — Manufacturing operations have only just commenced at the new Chennai plant, and the licensable firearm components business to be run through INDO-MIM Arms Components Private Limited depends on a Ministry of Home Affairs manufacturing licence that had not yet been applied for as at the report - the Company states it 'would make necessary application ... shortly'. Revenue from this vertical is gated on an approval outside the Company's control.
- Loss-making overseas subsidiaries and acquisition-integration risk — The Company has grown capacity inorganically (TRIAX Industries LLC in FY21, Conway Marsh Garrett Technologies in June 2023, Phoenix DeVentures II Inc in 2025) and states an intent to venture further into allied technologies organically or by acquisition. Form AOC-1 shows several of these wholly owned subsidiaries carrying losses before taxation, so integration and turnaround of acquired units is a live structural exposure.
- Natural calamity and physical asset risk — Machinery, stock and premises are insured against fire and other natural calamities and stock in transit is covered by a marine policy, with the coverage considered adequate; the Company notes its facilities are not located in an identified natural calamity zone. The exposure is mitigated by insurance rather than eliminated.
